Elena — congrats and welcome aboard!

I've attached a sprint-style MAP (BP_MAP_v1.xlsx) that embeds the post-signature implementation plan you asked for. High level summary below and in the sheet:

Week 0 (prep, 3 business days):
- Accounts & keys: Redwood will provision API keys for your staging account and add RBAC for the infra team.
- Secure onboarding call to verify network/VPC access and KMS integration.
- Shared Drive: initial folder with eval prompts and training materials.

Weeks 1–2 (staging integration + evals):
- Deploy model variant to staging (quantization profile A).
- Run evaluation suite against your canonical 10 prompts (see evaluation-prompts.md).
- Measure latency/throughput and iteration backlog.

Weeks 3–4 (canary + training):
- Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in production region US-WEST.
- Daily monitoring dashboards & automated rollback thresholds (error rate > 2% OR latency p50 > 400ms for 3 consecutive hours).
- Two live training sessions (developers, product owners) + follow-up recordings.

Weeks 5–8 (ramp & migration):
- Progressive ramp (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with quality gates after each step.
- Migration playbook for data stores and prefix caching warm-up.
- Final validation runbook and a 48-hour monitoring SLA post 100% cutover.

Success metrics we propose to track:
- Prompt-level accuracy/regression rate <= 3% relative to staging baseline
- Average cost per 1k tokens within agreed budget band
- Error rate and p99 latency within agreed SLOs

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the internal stakeholders for training (names + emails)?
2) Confirm if the 5% canary window fits your traffic model or if you prefer sampling by account instead.
3) We'll schedule the prep call — I'm available Wed/Thu this week.

I've CC'd Dev for the technical details and Marcus for rollout coordination. Attachment: BP_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Mina Haddad

Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / team —

Thanks for the MAP draft, Mina — a few clarifications and technical notes from the SE side:

1) Canary mechanics:
- We'll use request-sampling at the edge keyed by session id (recommended) to ensure representative user mix. We can switch to account-based targeting if you have sticky session constraints.
- We'll provision a dedicated pool with 2x worker headroom during canary to avoid cross-traffic interference.

2) Evaluation plan: attached evaluation-prompts.md contains the 10 prompts we're proposing to run under several temperature/beam settings. I recommend we run 500 examples per prompt during staging and 1k for canary sampling to get more stable signal.

3) Rollback criteria (technical):
- Continuous regression alert when prompt accuracy drops by > 4% on the sentinel prompt set for a 30-minute window.
- Token-explosion guard: abort if avg token generation per request > baseline * 1.5.

4) Migration notes: prefix/KV cache warm-up — we'll run synthetic traffic to warm KV slots before accepting live requests. Expect a 2–4 hour warm-up depending on your distribution.

5) Training: two 75-minute sessions (Dev & Product track). We can provide lab exercises and a short post-training quiz to certify engineers who will manage cutovers.

Action items I can take this week:
- Upload evaluation-prompts.md to the shared Drive and run a dry-run on your dev dataset.
- Open Jira tickets for canary automation and rollback runbook.

Elena — could you confirm if BluePeak has an on-call rotation we should hook into for the two-week canary window?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: evaluation-prompts.md (text)
